note: Curated links that cannot be derived from the source data: which n8n workflows touch which contracts and products, which apps integrate which product, which risks affect which agent families. Everything else in the graph is derived from the Sub4Me, Skill Marketplace, Control Tower and n8n sample data. Fictional.

tours.title: Ariba renewal
tours.summary: From one customer to a contract, its offer, automation, skills and governance.

steps.title: One customer
steps.text: Muster Industrie AG is the centre of the Sub4Me data: contracts, offers, tickets and AI-unit consumption hang off it.

steps.title: A contract that ends soon
steps.text: Ariba Procurement runs until 2027-01-31 and the notice deadline is close. Everything around it lights up when you ask for the impact.

steps.title: The renewal offer
steps.text: SAP offered a two-year renewal. The offer renews the contract and is tied to the same product.

steps.title: Automation that watches it
steps.text: An n8n workflow reminds the account team about renewals, so a change here also touches automation.

steps.title: Skills that read the data
steps.text: Skills such as renewal-radar and customer-call-prep use the Sub4Me tools and serve the same customer.

steps.title: Governance on the other side
steps.text: Switch the view and the same graph shows risks and agents: overprivileged agents are tied to risk R2 and to the access review skill.

tours.title: AI governance
tours.summary: Two risks, one agent that sits in both, and the skills that help.

steps.title: Risk R2: overprivileged agents
steps.text: The CISO owns this high risk (progress 35%, due Dec 2026). Impact mode shows the seven agent families whose identities hold more rights than they need.

steps.title: One agent, two risks
steps.text: Contract Drafter is tied to R2 and to the EU AI Act risk. Where risks overlap, one fix pays twice, and one miss hurts twice.

steps.title: Risk R6: EU AI Act
steps.text: General Counsel owns this one (progress 44%, due 12 Dec 2026). It touches the agents that classify contracts, draft replies and run onboarding or rosters.

steps.title: A skill that closes the gap
steps.text: access-review-prep reads the overprivileged-agent data through the connector tools and is linked to R2 and R7. It is still a pilot and owned by Platform Security.

steps.title: From findings to the board
steps.text: board-briefing turns risks, agents and budget into a one-page briefing and is linked to the EU AI Act risk. access-review-prep depends on it, so the chain ends with a decision-ready summary.
